pipeline_embedded.summary: The embedded (Case 2) builder in AUX is D:/WEB_AUX/aux_web_version/backend/builders/embedded_builder.py, consumed only by backend/pipeline_embedded.py. It produces three payloads: (1) build_embedded_schema_payload, a superset of the standalone BC-create payload with top-level keys activityTrackingInfos, entityDeployments, entityMetadatas, lookupBERelations (empty), relatedLookups (empty), and viewResourceInfos; (2) build_relation_payload, a BERelations wrapper that links the child BC to its parent via two BERelationFields (parent DomainCode-like field mapped to child domaincodeEx, and the parent FK field mapped to an identically named child field) with cardinality MANYTOONE and relationType "child"; (3) build_embedded_deploy_payload, a two-step deploy body (stepA/stepB) with a hardcoded datastore URI. The parent BC is referenced purely by registry data (qad_entity_registry.get_entity): entity_code such as "SalesOrderHeaders" becomes relatedEntityCode and the registry's urn:be:... URI becomes relatedEntityURI; the parent's domain field is discovered by scanning the registry pk_fields for a name containing "domain", falling back to "DomainCode". Versus a standalone BC, the embedded schema payload differs in: table name is "xx"+lowercase BC name instead of the PascalCase BC name; field codes are used raw (no sql_safe, no display-label derivation, fieldLabel = code); each field carries roughly 20 extra keys (modelId sequence starting at 4, qNewRec, translationType, suitableDataType, overrideContextType="Domain" for domaincodeEx, a percent-encoded IEntityDeployment per-field uri, etc.); entityTables is populated (with plural jsonName and comma-joined tableKeyFields) instead of empty; isBusinessDocument is False with empty bdocumentURI/bdocumentCode; embedded-only flags isDataExtensionOnly=True and isDataExtensionEnable=True are set; and a viewResourceInfos block (isVirtualBE=True, existingForm/existingGridForm "No", parentEntity "none") is included. Child PK design is deliberate: no SeqNumber is injected by the builder; the child PK is the parent FK field plus domaincodeEx, both supplied upstream by the EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR LLM step. A dated code comment records that the panel-vs-grid rendering is inherent to MANYTOONE cardinality and that isEmbedded=False / isUseInBusinessDocument=True are the known-working relation defaults. view_builder.py and form_builder.py contain no embedded/parent-specific branches at all (only null relation placeholder keys and parentURI:None); the embedded pipeline never builds a custom view or form for the child. Hardcoded identity values (module com.extensions.customapp, app name CustomApp, datastore urn:datastore:com.extensions.extension, and a percent-encoded module literal baked into two URI f-strings) are all stale for the new environment. One likely latent bug: embedded field codes skip sql_safe but build_data_lists keys the dropdown field_list_map by sql_safe(code), so a reserved-word dropdown field would never get its dataListCode patched.

pipeline_embedded_2.summary: The AUX embedded (Case 2) flow uses exactly three LLM prompts, all defined in D:/WEB_AUX/aux_web_version/backend/agents/prompts.py and invoked from backend/pipeline_embedded.py: EMBEDDED_REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING (lines 391-451), EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR (lines 453-515), and the shared VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR (lines 100-155). Unlike the standalone flow, the embedded requirements agent outputs raw JSON directly (parent_entity_key, bc_pascal, wants_separate_view, child_pk, custom_fields), not plain text. The embedded field creator then emits the final spec JSON with a mandated three-part PK ordering: domaincodeEx (character), the parent FK field (injected by the pipeline from an entity registry), then a child-specific PK that must NOT be part of the FK, per the QAD rule quoted in the prompt that the extension entity's full PK cannot be contained in the N-1 relation's foreign key. The embedded flow performs NO form planning, event handler, or TypeScript generation: FORM_PLANNER, FORM_FIELD_BUILDER, EVENT_HANDLER_PLANNER, TS_CODE_WRITER, and TS_COMPILER are never invoked by pipeline_embedded.py; after step 2 the pipeline is pure QAD API orchestration (metadata POST, dropdown wiring GET+POST, BERelation POST, deploy check, deploy, optional view registration). Crucially, the embedded prompts contain ZERO hardcoded com.extensions.customapp identities: the only 4 occurrences in prompts.py (lines 259, 265, 266, 326) are all inside the standalone TS_CODE_WRITER; the embedded flow's identity hardcoding lives instead in builders/embedded_builder.py (MODULE constant line 13, dataStoreURI urn:datastore:com.extensions.extension line 337) and in pipeline_embedded.py's completion summary (line 363). Both embedded prompts carry a {QAD_DOCS_CONTEXT} placeholder filled from the "business_component" docs bundle via .replace (not .format, because the templates contain literal JSON braces), and the requirements prompt additionally has {ENTITY_MENU} filled from the live entity registry. Field code conventions differ between flows: embedded custom fields are PascalCase with reserved-word renames status→StatusCode/date→FieldDate/type→FieldType, while standalone fields are camelCase with a much larger rename table. The requirements prompt's allowed type list omits datetime-tz, percent, and url, which the standalone prompt supports. The pipeline has a Python safety guard (pipeline_embedded.py:132-149) that injects a fallback child PK at index 2 if the LLM omits it. The Adaptive port (D:/WEB_AUX/adaptive_java_version/backend/agents/prompts.py) carries 8 prompt names, all standalone (REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING, FIELD_CREATOR, VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR, FORM_PLANNER, FORM_FIELD_BUILDER, EVENT_HANDLER_PLANNER, TS_CODE_WRITER, TS_COMPILER); neither EMBEDDED_* prompt exists there (grep for EMBEDDED/domaincodeEx/parent_entity returns nothing), so both must be ported for Case 2, while VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR is already present. All three embedded LLM calls use MODEL_MATRIX["generation"] (gpt-4o) with json_mode=True.

facts.fact: The embedded pipeline imports exactly three prompts from agents/prompts.py: EMBEDDED_REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING, EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR, VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR

EMBEDDED_REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING (prompts.py lines 391-451) asks the model to output raw JSON with keys parent_entity_key, bc_pascal, description, wants_separate_view, child_pk {code, dataType}, custom_fields [{code, dataType, dropdown_values?}] - JSON output, unlike the standalone REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING which forbids JSON and outputs plain text

EMBEDDED_REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING contains two placeholders: {QAD_DOCS_CONTEXT} (line 403) and {ENTITY_MENU} (line 406), substituted at runtime with str.replace, deliberately not .format because the template contains literal JSON braces
{QAD_DOCS_CONTEXT} is filled from docs bundle 'business_component' via docs_loader.get_bundle, prefixed with '## QAD Platform Reference Docs'; empty string when the bundle is empty
{ENTITY_MENU} is filled from entity_menu_for_prompt() in qad_entity_registry, i.e. the parent-entity list shown to the LLM is a live registry, not text baked into the prompt

Embedded requirements prompt allowed field types: character, integer, int64, decimal, date, datetime, logical, dropdown, dropdown_integer, dropdown_int64, dropdown_logical - it omits datetime-tz, percent, and url which the standalone REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING allows (prompts.py:24)

Child PK rules in EMBEDDED_REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING: FK fields (domaincodeEx + parent FK) are injected automatically; the child PK must never be domaincodeEx, DomainCode, or the parent FK field; one-record-per-parent BCs use a character field '<BCName>Code' defaulting to 'DEFAULT'; multi-row BCs use an integer 'LineNumber' or 'SeqNumber'

The requirements agent is forbidden from asking questions (must assume), custom_fields must exclude DomainCode/domaincodeEx/parent FK/child_pk, and wants_separate_view is true only when the user explicitly mentions a separate view, standalone view, menu entry, or browse screen

dropdown_values (snake_case key) is mandatory in the requirements output for every dropdown-family field: min 2, max 20 {code,label} pairs, first value becomes the default; the field-creator output uses the camelCase key dropdownValues instead

EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR (prompts.py lines 453-515) receives requirements JSON plus fk_field and fk_type 'provided by the system', and outputs {"status":"ok","spec":{bc_pascal,description,fields[]}} JSON with mandated PK order: 1) domaincodeEx character isPrimary, 2) <fk_field> <fk_type> isPrimary, 3) <child_pk> isPrimary, then custom fields isPrimary:false

fk_field and fk_type are injected by the pipeline into the field-creator user message from the entity registry entry (entity_info['fk_field'], entity_info['fk_type']) resolved via get_entity(parent_entity_key)

EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR embeds the QAD platform rule verbatim: 'Full primary key of Extension-entity cannot be contained in the foreign key of N-1 relation' - fields 1+2 form the FK, field 3 breaks the constraint, and without it QAD rejects the BERelation

Embedded custom-field code rules are PascalCase with Hungarian-prefix stripping and reserved-word renames status→StatusCode, date→FieldDate, type→FieldType - different from the standalone FIELD_CREATOR which mandates camelCase and a ~26-entry rename table (e.g. status→statusCode)

The literal field code 'domaincodeEx' (lowercase d, capital E) is hardcoded in the EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR prompt text as the mandatory first PK, dataType character - this is the only identity-like hardcoded value inside the embedded prompts

The embedded prompts contain ZERO occurrences of com.extensions.customapp; grep of prompts.py finds exactly 4 occurrences, all inside the standalone TS_CODE_WRITER: module declaration (259), DTO import (265), Constants import (266), NgData grid key _com_extensions_customapp_{BCName}Lines (326)

The embedded flow's identity hardcoding lives in the builder layer instead of prompts: MODULE = "com.extensions.customapp" and dataStoreURI "urn:datastore:com.extensions.extension" in embedded_builder.py, plus "module": "com.extensions.customapp" in the pipeline's completion summary

VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR (prompts.py:100-155) is reused verbatim by the embedded flow's step 4 auto-fix; the user message concatenates requirements JSON, submitted spec JSON, and the QAD error (submitResult); output is {"status":"fixed",fix_summary,spec} or {"status":"failed",reason}; on 'fixed' the pipeline retries BC creation once with the corrected spec

VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR's fixable-error list is standalone-oriented (camelCase reserved-word renames, maxLength default 80) and contains no embedded-specific guardrails such as 'never rename domaincodeEx or the FK field'; a 'fix' that renames a PK/FK field would silently break the BERelation step

The embedded flow invokes NO form/eventhandler/TS prompts: FORM_PLANNER, FORM_FIELD_BUILDER, EVENT_HANDLER_PLANNER, TS_CODE_WRITER, TS_COMPILER never appear in pipeline_embedded.py; after step 2 everything is deterministic QAD API orchestration, and the completion summary hardcodes panel_count 0 and empty panels

Python safety guard after the field-creator call: if no PK field exists whose code is neither domaincodeex nor the fk_field (case-insensitive), the pipeline injects a fallback child PK at index 2 using requirements.child_pk or '<bc_pascal>Code' character isPrimary/isRequired true
All three embedded LLM calls use MODEL_MATRIX['generation'] which maps to 'gpt-4o', with json_mode=True; _llm and _parse_json_output are imported from the standalone pipeline module

The Adaptive port's prompts.py defines exactly 8 top-level prompt names, all standalone: REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING (38), FIELD_CREATOR (106), VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR (190), FORM_PLANNER (249), FORM_FIELD_BUILDER (275), EVENT_HANDLER_PLANNER (310), TS_CODE_WRITER (339), TS_COMPILER (490)

Neither EMBEDDED_REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING nor EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR exists in the Adaptive port; grep for EMBEDDED/embedded/domaincodeEx/parent_entity in adaptive prompts.py returns zero matches - both embedded prompts must be ported for Case 2, while VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR (the third embedded-flow prompt) is already ported

Embedded pipeline is 7 base steps growing to 8 when wants_separate_view is true (step 8 = standalone view registration via view_builder.build_view_payload, no LLM involved); step labels: 1 requirements, 2 field design, 3 metadata, 4 duplicate/auto-fix, 5 relations to parent, 6 warnings check, 7 deploy, 8 view registration

Dropdown wiring is a non-LLM step 3.5: after BC creation, the pipeline GETs the entity (response wrapped in {"data":{...}}), patches each dropdown field's dataListCode and defaultValue via patch_dropdown_fields (imported from bc_builder, shared with standalone), and POSTs the enriched entity back

bc_pascal naming constraint for embedded BCs: PascalCase, max 32 chars, no spaces (stated in requirements prompt); standalone abbreviation table (Notification→Notif etc., prompts.py:18-20) is NOT repeated in the embedded prompt

model_calls.purpose: Parse the user's free-text request into JSON: parent entity choice, BC name, child PK, custom fields with dropdown values, separate-view flag
Turn requirements + system-injected fk_field/fk_type into the final field spec JSON with the domaincodeEx/FK/child-PK ordering

model_calls.step: Step 4 - Handling duplicates & auto-fix (conditional, only on QAD error)
model_calls.purpose: Given requirements + submitted spec + QAD error JSON, either emit a corrected spec (status fixed, one retry) or status failed with a reason

endpoints.purpose: Create embedded BC metadata (also the retry path after auto-fix)
Fetch freshly-enriched entity for dropdown wiring; response wrapped in {"data":{...}}
Second POST setting dataListCode + defaultValue on each dropdown field
endpoints.payload_shape: the GET-returned entity dict mutated by patch_dropdown_fields(enriched, field_list_map)

endpoints.purpose: Register the N-1 relation from the embedded BC to the parent entity
Pre-deploy warnings check
Deploy the embedded business entity
Optional step 8: register a standalone view/menu entry when wants_separate_view

pipeline_embedded_2_2.summary: This subsystem is AUX's deterministic Progress-ABL ingestion path: progress_parser.py parses raw .p/.cls source text (attached or pasted into the prompt, never schema dumps) into a structured dict of temp-tables/fields/PK/procedures/functions, lookup_detector.py scans the same source for FIND/FOR-EACH...WHERE constructs and classifies each as a static/dependent/uncertain lookup candidate via a 4-rule confidence registry with bounded backward variable tracing, and lookup_generator.py turns STATIC candidates into a best-effort QAD Lookup Definition POST payload that is dry-run only (never actually POSTed by the pipeline). Critically for Case 2: this entire subsystem is invoked ONLY in the standard (non-embedded) mode. routers/client_extensions.py:129 gates the parser behind `if req.mode != "embedded"`, the code comment explicitly says embedded mode "doesn't currently benefit (it picks a parent entity from a fixed registry)", and pipeline_embedded.py contains zero references to any of these modules. In the standard flow the parser output replaces the REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING LLM call (step 1 skipped), feeds FIELD_CREATOR as pre-built requirements text, and detected lookup candidates are re-hydrated in pipeline.py after view registration (step 13) to emit lookup_candidate/lookup_needs_review/lookup_summary SSE events via create_lookup(dry_run=True). progress_parser.py and lookup_detector.py are environment-neutral pure text processing with no QAD identity or network dependency. lookup_generator.py and its pipeline caller are heavily OLD-environment dependent: the endpoint is appended to {base}/qad-central/api/qracore/ (new env has no /qad-central/), and pipeline.py hardcodes the stale com.extensions.customapp identity into lookup metadata, the run summary, and the auto-registered entity URI. Beyond the known fieldSet lowercasing at lookup_generator.py:142-145, three more case-transform-against-evidence smells exist: fieldLabel titlecasing (line 125) versus the reference record's preserved "mfg-colorcode", browseName titlecasing of the source table (line 134), and a three-way operator-casing inconsistency ("eq" lowercase at line 229 vs "EQ" uppercase from _map_operator vs UI "equals", plus "LITERAL" vs UI "Literal"). The tests document real regressions previously caught in review (attribute-colon truncation, clause keywords/AND inside string literals, word operators) and prove fail-soft behavior throughout — the detector swallows ALL exceptions and returns [], and the parser converts every problem into parse_warnings.

facts.fact: progress_parser.parse_progress_file accepts raw ABL text OR a Path to a .p/.cls file; input is Progress ABL source code, not schema dumps. Distinguishes .cls vs .p purely by filename extension.

Parser output is a dict: {source_type, tables[{name, fields[{name,type,label,format,required,qad_type}], primary_key[]}], procedures[], functions[], source_tables_referenced[], lookups[] (LookupCandidate.to_dict), parse_warnings[]}. It never raises; malformed ABL becomes parse_warnings entries.

ABL-to-QAD type map covers 17 ABL types collapsing to 6 QAD types (character/integer/decimal/logical/date/datetime); BLOB/CLOB/RAW/MEMPTR map to character with a lossy-mapping warning; unknown types default to character with a warning.

Parser strategy is comment-stripped case-insensitive regex extraction (no grammar). Only /* */ block comments are stripped; OpenEdge // single-line comments are NOT handled, so keywords in // comments would confuse extractors.

TEMP-TABLE field extraction requires the exact shape 'FIELD name AS type'; fields declared with LIKE, EXTENT arrays, or DEFINE ... LIKE are not extracted (no regex for them exists anywhere in the file).

Temp-table block end is found via the next structural boundary (next DEFINE/PROCEDURE/FUNCTION/CLASS/METHOD) rather than the next period, because ABL statements span lines and embed periods in literals.

Fields listed in an 'IS PRIMARY' INDEX become primary_key and get required=True; per-field FORMAT and LABEL are read from a look-ahead window bounded by the next FIELD/INDEX keyword; missing LABEL is auto-titlecased from the identifier, missing FORMAT gets QAD defaults (character x(80) etc.).

.cls files become one synthetic 'table' whose fields are DEFINE PUBLIC PROPERTY declarations; only METHOD PUBLIC methods are collected (PROTECTED/PRIVATE excluded, verified by test); class name is the last dotted segment.

parsed_to_requirements_text renders ONLY the FIRST temp-table as the BC subject ('typically only' per comment); any additional temp-tables in the file are parsed but silently dropped from the requirements text.

parsed_to_requirements_text emits the exact numbered-list shape REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING would output (BC purpose/BC name/Field count/Fields with pk/required/max-length), so FIELD_CREATOR can consume it directly and step 1 is skipped. An explicit BC name in the user note (regex on 'named?...') wins over the table-derived name to avoid re-run collisions; table names are PascalCased after stripping a leading 'tt' prefix.

The _EXPLICIT_NAME_RE regex matches the word 'name'/'named' anywhere in the user note, so a note like 'the field name is X' would incorrectly capture X as the BC name (no anchoring to 'BC'/'component').

lookup_detector.detect_lookups takes raw .p source (string), returns list[LookupCandidate] ordered by source line; each candidate has source_table, target_field, classification (static|dependent|uncertain), confidence 0-1, filters[], result_field (ALWAYS empty string, see browse-identity gap), evidence_line (1-based, mapped to ORIGINAL source via offset-preserving comment strip), matched_rule, notes.

detect_lookups swallows ALL exceptions and returns [] ('detection must never break parsing') — a deliberate silent-failure mode: a detector crash on a real file produces zero candidates with no warning.

Detection is a registry of 4 filter-classifier rules run per WHERE filter with highest-confidence-wins: rule1 literal in WHERE (0.95 string / 0.92 numeric -> static), rule2 variable traced to local literal (0.85 direct assignment / 0.70 DEFINE...INITIAL -> static), rule3 cascading screen-field dependency (0.60-0.85 -> dependent; covers INPUT x, x:SCREEN-VALUE, SELF/THIS-OBJECT getters, screen-field names, values populated by an earlier FIND i.e. chained lookups, and expressions referencing screen fields), rule4 fallback unresolvable (0.30 -> uncertain, never dropped).

Backward tracing is bounded to the enclosing PROCEDURE/FUNCTION/METHOD body with a hard 4000-character lookback floor — values assigned outside the block or passed as parameters resolve to 'uncertain' (verified by test Case5: an INPUT PARAMETER filter is uncertain).

Candidate aggregation is worst-case across filters (dependent > uncertain > static); confidence and matched_rule come from the highest-confidence filter in the worst class; for dependent lookups target_field is the driving filter's column, otherwise the first filter's column.

result_field is always left blank because a bare FIND/FOR selects the whole record — the returned column is unknowable from source alone ('browse-identity gap'); the generator flags it in _needs_verification.

Quote-masking (_mask_quotes) protects three scans from operator/keyword tokens inside string literals: AND-splitting of filters, trailing-clause truncation (NO-LOCK/USE-INDEX/BY/WHILE/OF...), and operator location. Tests Case9/Case10 are explicit regressions for 'BY'/'BILL OF LADING' and 'SMITH AND SONS' literals (marked 'review MED').

Statement-end detection distinguishes a block-opening ':' (followed by whitespace) from an attribute-access ':' (fld:SCREEN-VALUE); test Case8 is the regression (marked 'review HIGH') where an inline field:SCREEN-VALUE filter was previously truncated at the colon and misclassified uncertain instead of dependent.

WHERE filters are split ONLY on AND; OR is not a separator and is not handled — an 'a = 1 OR b = 2' body would be parsed as a single condition and misparse at the first '=' into a garbage RHS, landing in rule4/uncertain rather than being modeled.

ABL word operators EQ/NE/GT/LT/GE/LE and BEGINS/MATCHES/CONTAINS are recognized alongside symbolic ops (longest-first so <=/>=/<> don't split); test Case11 ('review MED' regression) proves EQ filters were previously dropped.

Screen fields are collected from UPDATE/SET/PROMPT-FOR/FORM/DISPLAY ... WITH FRAME|BROWSE statements minus a hardcoded stopword list; identifiers are lowercased for membership tests, so screen-field matching is case-insensitive.

build_lookup_warnings emits one parse_warning per dependent ('Configure manually in QAD's Lookup Definitions using a Qualifier (Type: Field)') or uncertain candidate; static candidates produce no warning (surfaced via pipeline SSE events instead).

lookup_generator.generate_lookup_payload accepts ONLY static candidates (raises LookupGenerationError otherwise) plus bc_metadata {namespace, app, bc_name, module_uri, app_name, field_label?, data_type?, browse_uri?, browse_entity?, browse_label?, result_field?, search_field?, field_set?}; returns {lookups:[obj], _needs_verification:[...]} where _-prefixed keys are stripped before any POST.

The lookup payload wire keys are camelCase (appName, browseName, browseURI, fieldLabel, fieldSet, moduleURI, namespace, reference, resultField, searchField, searchFieldOperator, lookupQualifiers, lookupResultFields, lookupSearchConditions); top-level uri, modelId, concurrencyHash are DELIBERATELY OMITTED on create as unconfirmed.

A confirmed reference record (real static lookup read from QAD's Lookup Definitions UI 2026-07-28, OLD env, com.extensions.sdapp identity) establishes: reference is empty, lookupQualifiers and lookupResultFields are empty for static lookups, resultField/searchField/condition fieldName are DOTTED <browseEntity>.<field> paths never bare source columns, browseURI form is urn:browse:bebrowse:<module.path>.<browseName>, and the Field URI suffix is the PHYSICAL table + field with ORIGINAL case (xx_itemextsd.ColorCoded).

The reference record explicitly does NOT settle wire-level operator casing ('equals' vs 'eq'/'EQ', 'Literal' vs 'LITERAL') because it is a UI reading; the docstring says the actual POST body from the browser Network tab is needed before dry_run=False is safe.

_map_operator: only exact CONTAINS is confirmed; BEGINS/MATCHES are collapsed to CONTAINS (a SEMANTIC broadening from prefix/wildcard to substring, flagged unconfirmed); '=' maps to 'EQ' unconfirmed; anything else passes through uppercased unconfirmed.

KNOWN SMELL (given): fieldSet is mechanically built as urn:field:{ns}.{app}.{bc}.I{bc}:{bc.lower()}.{field.lower()} — lowercasing both suffix parts against the reference record's original-case evidence; the code itself flags this in _needs_verification.

SAME SMELL #2: fieldLabel falls back to _titlecase(target_field) (e.g. 'colorCoded' -> 'Color Coded') while the reference record shows Field Label preserved verbatim as 'mfg-colorcode' — a case/format transform against evidence.

SAME SMELL #3: browseName defaults to _titlecase(candidate.source_table) (e.g. 'abs_mstr' -> 'Abs Mstr') — fabricating a display name by case-transforming the physical table; flagged best-effort but still a transform not grounded in evidence.

SAME SMELL #4 (casing inconsistency within one payload): searchFieldOperator is hardcoded lowercase 'eq' while lookupSearchConditions.operator comes out UPPERCASE ('EQ'/'CONTAINS') from _map_operator, and fieldValue1Type is 'LITERAL' vs UI-shown 'Literal' — three different casings for operator-like enums in the same payload, all unverified on the wire.

create_lookup defaults to dry_run=True and uses identity-check 'if dry_run is not False' so ONLY an explicit False reaches the live POST (defense-in-depth); dry-run logs the payload and returns without network. The live path imports get_token/post_qad from qad_client and logs the full response for validating uncertain fields.

Embedded runs invoke run_embedded_pipeline(req.message) with the raw message; no parsed_requirements, no lookup_candidates, no parse_warnings. Standard-flow invocation chain: client_extensions.run() extracts .p/.cls source (attachment marker 'File: <name>.p\n\n<content>' from ClientExtPanel.tsx:81, OR pasted source recognized by >=2 of 10 ABL-signal regexes), calls parse_progress_file + parsed_to_requirements_text, streams parse_warnings as 'warning' SSE events before step 1, and passes parsed_requirements + lookup_candidates into run_pipeline. A parser exception never blocks the run (falls back to LLM step 1).

In run_pipeline, lookup candidates are re-hydrated via LookupCandidate.from_dict and emitted AFTER view registration (step 13) and BEFORE deploy (step 14): static -> 'lookup_candidate' SSE with dry-run payload (plus 'lookup_needs_review' reason=payload_gap when _needs_verification is non-empty); dependent/uncertain -> 'lookup_needs_review'; then a 'lookup_summary' event; counts land in summary['lookups']. pipeline_embedded_2_2_2.summary: The embedded (Case 2 / client-extensions) flow in AUX is served by backend/routers/client_extensions.py: a single SSE endpoint POST /api/run takes {message, run_id?, mode} and, when mode=="embedded", dispatches to run_embedded_pipeline(req.message) instead of the standalone pipeline; the deterministic Progress-file parser is deliberately skipped for embedded runs because the parent is chosen from a fixed registry. The frontend also uses GET /api/entities to list eligible parent entities (durable SQLite parent_entities table first, in-memory registry cache as fallback) and GET/DELETE /api/history for run history. qad_entity_registry.py holds 5 hand-authored built-in QAD standard parents (SalesOrderHeaders, PurchaseOrderHeaders, ItemMaster, InventoryMaster, WorkOrderMaster), each with a urn:be:com.qad.* URI, ordered PascalCase pk_fields, a single fk_field (the business key, never DomainCode), fk_type, and a description used in an LLM menu for parent matching; custom parents created by the standalone pipeline are write-through persisted and rehydrated at startup, with a one-time backfill from run history that hardcodes the stale com.extensions.customapp module. probe_parent_eh.py is a standalone stdout-only script probing the event-handler UPDATE flow (GET eventhandler by appURI/viewURI/type/appliesTo, then POST back a no-op with concurrencyHash, trying payload Shape A with uri then Shape B without, then re-GET to see if the hash changed) against the stale urn:app:com.extensions.customapp identity and the QAD-standard SalesOrders view. On Q-L: I found no evidence it ever ran — it writes no files, uses no logger, is untracked in git, is referenced nowhere else in the repo, PROGRESS.md never mentions it (and as of its 2026-07-28 entries still lists uri/modelId/concurrencyHash as unconfirmed), and app.log contains only POSTs to the eventhandler endpoint (pipeline creations), no GETs. Auth: the FastAPI routes themselves carry no authentication; QAD auth happens inside pipelines via OAuth2 password-grant bearer tokens (fetched fresh per use, never cached) at /qad-central/oauth/token, with a separate JSESSIONID form login at /qad-central/api/login used only by the SSS upload path; both /qad-central/ paths and the qracore API prefix are hardcoded and therefore stale for the new no-/qad-central environment.

facts.fact: POST /api/run is the single pipeline endpoint for BOTH standalone and embedded modes; RunRequest.mode == "embedded" selects run_embedded_pipeline(req.message), else run_pipeline with parsed requirements/lookups
RunRequest shape is {message: str (max-length capped), run_id: Optional[str], mode: str = "standard"}
/api/run is rate-limited to 5/minute because each run spawns 8 LLM calls
The deterministic Progress (.p/.cls) parser is explicitly skipped in embedded mode: "Embedded mode doesn't currently benefit (it picks a parent entity from a fixed registry)"

/api/run responds with an SSE StreamingResponse (text/event-stream, Cache-Control no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering no); event types observed: warning (standard mode only), step, error, complete (carries summary), and a final run_id event emitted unconditionally after the pipeline ends
Embedded pipeline SSE events carry {type, step, status, message, total} with BASE_TOTAL_STEPS = 7, growing to 8 when the user wants a separate view (wants_separate_view)

Embedded pipeline step names: 1 analyse requirements, 2 identify fields/PKs, 3 create embedded BC (+dropdown wiring), 4 conflict check/auto-fix, 5 build relation, 6 deployment warnings check, 7 deploy Business Entity, optional 8 register standalone view

Every run (embedded included) is saved to history as HistoryItem {id, created_at, user_input, bc_pascal, description, field_count, panel_count, status, summary_json, error_message, mode}; save failures are logged, never fail the request
History routes: GET /api/history (list), GET /api/history/{run_id} (404 if missing), DELETE /api/history/{run_id} (returns {ok:true}, 404 if missing)

GET /api/entities returns every registered parent entity for embedded BCs; tries durable DB (list_parent_entities) first, falls back to in-memory registry cache on DB failure; each item is {entity_code, uri, pk_fields, fk_field, fk_type, description, source}
The registry contains exactly 5 built-in QAD standard parents: SalesOrderHeaders, PurchaseOrderHeaders, ItemMaster, InventoryMaster, WorkOrderMaster

Built-in URIs: SalesOrderHeaders=urn:be:com.qad.sales.salesorder.ISalesOrderHeader, PurchaseOrderHeaders=urn:be:com.qad.purchasing.purchaseorders.IPurchaseOrderHeader, ItemMaster=urn:be:com.qad.base.item.IItem, InventoryMaster=urn:be:com.qad.inventory.inv.IInventoryMaster, WorkOrderMaster=urn:be:com.qad.pushproduction.workorder.IWorkOrderMaster

Per-entity metadata: uri (urn:be:...), pk_fields (PK field codes IN ORDER as QAD defines them, PascalCase, DomainCode first in all 5), fk_field (single FK the embedded child links on — the business key, NOT DomainCode), fk_type (character for all built-ins), description (human label shown to the LLM for matching), plus a source tag builtin|custom

Built-in entries are hand-authored in source code — the docstring gives instructions "HOW TO ADD A NEW BUILT-IN ENTRY (a genuine QAD standard BC)" with values taken from QAD entity metadata; there is no code that derives them from a live QAD query

The built-in URNs/PK codes were transcribed from the OLD QAD environment and are environment-specific in the sense that nothing verifies they exist in any given target; whether the same urn:be:com.qad.* URIs and PascalCase PK codes exist in the new eeadaptive environment is unverified

Durable source of truth is the SQLite parent_entities table (entity_code PK, uri, pk_fields as JSON array order-preserved, fk_field, fk_type default 'character', description, source default 'custom'); registry cache is hydrated from it at startup and written through on registration

The history backfill constructs custom-parent URIs as urn:be:{module}.{bc}.I{bc} with module defaulting to the hardcoded "com.extensions.customapp"

pipeline_embedded_2_2_2_2.summary: The embedded (Case 2) flow in AUX is a 7-step (optionally 8) SSE pipeline in backend/pipeline_embedded.py:run_embedded_pipeline(user_message), invoked from POST /api/run when RunRequest.mode == "embedded" (routers/client_extensions.py; main.py only mounts the router and seeds/hydrates the parent-entity registry at startup). It creates a child "extension" BC embedded under an existing parent BC: (1) LLM requirements gathering picks a parent_entity_key from a live registry menu injected into the prompt, names the BC, and identifies a child-specific PK; (2) LLM field creator emits a spec whose first three fields are the mandatory PK trio domaincodeEx + parent FK field + child PK, followed by custom fields; (3) POST of a full Entity Builder metadata payload to entitymetadatas; (4) on failure, one LLM auto-fix (VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR) and a single retry; (3.5, reported under step 3) GET-patch-POST round trip to wire dropdown fields to their data lists; (5) POST a BERelation payload (MANYTOONE, relationType "child", two BERelationFields mapping domaincodeEx->parent domain field and fk->fk) linking child to parent; (6) POST deployCheckForWarnings (response ignored); (7) POST deployBusinessEntity; (8, only if the user explicitly asked for a standalone view) POST viewResourceMetadatas using the same view_builder as the standalone flow. It makes 2 LLM calls normally (3 with auto-fix), needs only one user input (the free-text message; the parent is LLM-chosen from the registry, whose contents are served to the UI via GET /api/entities), and unlike the standalone flow builds no form, no event handlers, no TS code, no lookups, does not fast-fail duplicate BC names, and does not register the new BC as a future parent. Identity is hardcoded throughout as module com.extensions.customapp / app CustomApp / datastore urn:datastore:com.extensions.extension, and qad_client hardcodes the /qad-central/ path segment — all stale for the new environment. An untracked probe script (probe_parent_eh.py) shows in-progress exploration of GET-then-POST updates to an existing parent view's event handler (concurrencyHash round-trip), which is likely the next piece of embedded work not yet wired into any pipeline.

facts.fact: Embedded pipeline entry point is run_embedded_pipeline(user_message: str) -> AsyncGenerator of SSE strings; it takes ONLY the raw user message (no parsed requirements, no lookup candidates).
It is invoked from POST /api/run when RunRequest.mode == 'embedded'; the .p/.cls Progress-parser branch is explicitly skipped for embedded mode ('Embedded mode doesn't currently benefit').

main.py never calls the embedded pipeline directly; it mounts client_extensions_router (which owns /api/run) and at startup seeds builtin parent entities, one-time-backfills custom parents from successful standard-mode runs (gated by PRAGMA user_version, PARENT_BACKFILL_VERSION=1), and hydrates the in-memory registry from the parent_entities table.
The startup backfill only scans runs WHERE mode='standard', so BCs created by the embedded pipeline never become eligible parents.
/api/run is rate-limited to 5/minute; run history is saved to SQLite with mode='embedded' and a run_id SSE event is emitted after the pipeline finishes.

STEP SEQUENCE: base total is 7 steps, growing to 8 when requirements.wants_separate_view is true; labels are 1 Understanding Embedded BC requirements, 2 Designing Embedded BC fields, 3 Creating Business Component metadata, 4 Handling duplicates & auto-fix, 5 Building relations to parent entity, 6 Checking deployment warnings, 7 Deploying Business Component, 8 Registering standalone view in QAD.

Step 1 (LLM): EMBEDDED_REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING prompt gets two .replace() injections: {QAD_DOCS_CONTEXT} from docs_loader bundle 'business_component' and {ENTITY_MENU} from entity_menu_for_prompt() (live registry codes + descriptions); called with MODEL_MATRIX['generation'] and json_mode=True.

Step 1 output JSON shape: {parent_entity_key, bc_pascal, description, wants_separate_view, child_pk:{code,dataType}, custom_fields:[{code,dataType,dropdown_values?}]}; the prompt forbids asking questions and forbids including DomainCode/domaincodeEx/FK/child_pk inside custom_fields.
Parent resolution is local: get_entity(parent_entity_key) against the in-memory registry; unknown key aborts with an error listing supported_entity_codes() (live list, not hardcoded).

Builtin parent registry (5 entries) with old-env URIs: SalesOrderHeaders urn:be:com.qad.sales.salesorder.ISalesOrderHeader (FK SalesOrderNumber), PurchaseOrderHeaders urn:be:com.qad.purchasing.purchaseorders.IPurchaseOrderHeader (FK PurchaseOrderNumber), ItemMaster urn:be:com.qad.base.item.IItem (FK ItemCode), InventoryMaster urn:be:com.qad.inventory.inv.IInventoryMaster (FK ItemCode), WorkOrderMaster urn:be:com.qad.pushproduction.workorder.IWorkOrderMaster (FK WorkOrderNumber); each has pk_fields, fk_field, fk_type, description; all fk_type 'character'.

Registry is a durable-store-backed cache: parent_entities table is source of truth, hydrate() overlays persisted rows at startup, register_and_persist_custom_bc() write-throughs; infer_fk_field() = first PK that is not domaincode/domaincodeex.

Step 2 (LLM): EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR receives requirements JSON augmented with fk_field and fk_type from the registry entry; docs bundle 'business_component' injected; generation model, json_mode; output is {status,spec:{bc_pascal,description,fields:[...]}}.

Mandated PK structure (prompt): field 1 domaincodeEx (character, PK, required), field 2 <fk_field> (fk_type, PK, required), field 3 <child_pk> (PK, required, NOT part of FK), then custom fields non-PK; rationale quoted from QAD: full PK of extension entity cannot be contained in the FK of the N-1 relation.

Post-LLM safety guard: if no PK exists whose code is outside {domaincodeex, fk_field.lower()}, a fallback child PK is inserted at fields index 2 with code requirements.child_pk.code or '<bc_pascal>Code' and dataType from child_pk or 'character'.

Step 3 (QAD write): build_embedded_schema_payload(spec) then POST entitymetadatas?viewUri=urn:be:com.qad.qra.adapter.entity.IEntityBuilderCRUD; token fetched fresh via get_token() before every QAD call (no token caching anywhere in the flow).

Embedded schema payload top-level keys: activityTrackingInfos [{activityTracking:false}], entityDeployments, entityMetadatas, lookupBERelations:[], relatedLookups:[], viewResourceInfos; entity URI pattern urn:be:com.extensions.customapp.<BC>.I<BC>; physical table name 'xx' + bc lowercase; jsonName of table '<table>s'; per-field jsonName is camelCase of the field code (first letter lowered).

Embedded entityMetadata flags: bcType 'Standard', isDataExtensionEnable true, isDataExtensionOnly true, isBusinessDocument false, isQadStandard false, scope 'SYSTEM', allowBeRelations true, appName 'CustomApp', businessComponentStatus 'INITIAL'; viewResourceInfos entry has dataExtensionOnly true, isVirtualBE true, parentEntity 'none', existingForm/existingGridForm 'No'.

Per-field metadata: primaryKey is a 1-based ordinal for PK fields else null; isRequired forced true for PKs; overrideContextType 'Domain' only for field code 'domaincodeEx'; dropdown types map to a base suitableDataType via DROPDOWN_BASE_TYPE; field uri strings embed the percent-encoded module 'com%2Eextensions%2Ecustomapp'.

Step 4 (conditional LLM auto-fix): only when is_qad_success(bc_result) is false; VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR gets requirements+spec+QAD submitResult; on status 'fixed' the spec is replaced and step 3 retried EXACTLY ONCE; on 'failed' or exception the pipeline aborts. When the first POST succeeded, step 4 is emitted as done 'No conflicts — proceeding' BEFORE step 3's done event (event order 4-then-3).

Unlike the standalone pipeline, the embedded flow has NO duplicate-name fast-fail: _is_duplicate_entity_error and _qad_error_messages (pipeline.py:209-231, used at pipeline.py:447) are not imported or used in pipeline_embedded.py; embedded error events dump raw JSON of submitResult errors.

Step 3.5 (dropdown wiring, reported under step 3, runs only when field_list_map non-empty): GET entitymetadatas?entityURI=<urlencoded entity_uri>&viewUri=urn:be:com.qad.qra.adapter.entity.IEntityBuilderCRUD (response wrapped in {'data':{...}}, unwrapped), patch_dropdown_fields sets dataListCode+defaultValue on each dropdown field, then POST the enriched body back to the same endpoint; abort if GET has no entityMetadatas or POST not successful.

Data lists are built at payload time by build_data_lists(fields): one dataList per dropdown field ({dataListCode, dataListValues:[{dataValue,dataLabel}], serviceCall:''}); list code is the SQL-safe field code; default value is the first dropdown value's code; a dropdown field with no dropdownValues raises ValueError (deploy would fail).

Step 5 (QAD write): build_relation_payload(bc_pascal, fields, parent_entity_code, parent_entity_uri=registry uri, fk_field_code=registry fk_field) then POST berelation?viewUri=urn:be:com.qad.qra.berelation.IBERelation; aborts on failure.

BERelation payload: {supplementaryMessages:[], BERelations:[{...}]} with exactly two BERelationFields: (sourceFieldCode 'domaincodeEx' -> relatedFieldCode = parent's domain PK found by scanning parent pk_fields for 'domain' substring, default 'DomainCode') and (sourceFieldCode = relatedFieldCode = fk_field_code); cardinality 'MANYTOONE', relationType 'child', isExtension true, isEmbedded false, isUseInBusinessDocument true, isCascadeDelete false, isCascadeDeleteForBD true, isIncludeOnParent false, isLookup false, relationCode=relationLabel=bc_pascal, sourceAppName 'CustomApp'.
relationID is a hardcoded prefix '8c9676c6-0c12-13a3-f114-' plus 12 hex chars of a fresh uuid; relation uri is urn:be:com.qad.qra.berelation.IBERelation:<relationID>.

Documented experiment (2026-07-15): the embedded child always renders as a GRID on the parent form; the 'Composition Relation'/'Include Grid on Parent Form' flags cannot force a panel; a panel would require a ONETOONE redesign (child PK = domaincodeEx + parent FK only, no separate child identifier). Known-working defaults are isEmbedded=False, isUseInBusinessDocument=True.

Step 6 (QAD write): POST deployCheckForWarnings with stepA payload {entityURI, isInitialDataLoaded:false}; the RESPONSE IS NOT CHECKED (only transport exceptions abort) — warnings are effectively ignored.

Step 7 (QAD write): POST deployBusinessEntity with stepB payload {entityURI, appURI:'urn:app:com.extensions.customapp', dataStoreURI:'urn:datastore:com.extensions.extension', isInitialDataLoaded:false, allowActivityTracking:false}; checked with is_qad_success.

Step 8 (optional QAD write, only when wants_separate_view): reuses the STANDALONE view builder build_view_payload(spec) and POSTs viewResourceMetadatas?viewUri=urn:be:com.qad.qra.meta.IViewResourceMetadata; payload is a HYBRID_BROWSE viewResourceMetadata with browseView/maintView/hybridBrowseView, browseColumns from all fields, keyFields from PK fields, isEntityVirtual true.

Complete event summary: {bc_pascal, description, field_count, fields[{code,dataType,isPrimary,isRequired}], panel_count:0, panels:[], pk_codes, parent_entity, view_label, module:'com.extensions.customapp' (hardcoded literal)}; panel_count/panels are always empty because embedded builds no form.
The embedded flow does NOT auto-register the created BC into the parent registry; only the standalone pipeline calls register_and_persist_custom_bc after deploy.

Shared helpers imported from pipeline.py: _llm (AsyncOpenAI chat.completions, max_tokens=15000 unless model startswith 'gpt-5', optional response_format json_object), _parse_json_output (strips markdown fences and trims to outermost JSON braces), MODEL_MATRIX {'planning':'gpt-4o-mini','generation':'gpt-4o','compile':'gpt-4o-mini'}.

OpenAI client is constructed per-run from env OPENAI_API_KEY; both embedded LLM steps use MODEL_MATRIX['generation'] (gpt-4o) — embedded step 1 does NOT use the cheaper 'planning' model that standalone step 1 uses.

QAD transport: get_token() POSTs {base}/qad-central/oauth/token with client_id/username/password/grant_type=password AS URL QUERY PARAMS; post_qad/get_qad hit {base}/qad-central/api/qracore/<endpoint> with Bearer token; _handle() converts HTTP/non-JSON failures into {'error','raw'} envelopes; is_qad_success requires submitResult.success==true AND errorSeverity==0 AND empty errors.

Base URL comes from merged config qad_base_url() (.env QAD_BASE_URL with settings.json overrides and legacy qad_server_url fallback), re-read live on mtime change; the '/qad-central/' segment itself is hardcoded in qad_client.py.
SSE event schema (embedded): data: {type: step|error|complete, step, total (7 or 8, dynamic), name (from STEP_LABELS), status running|done|error, message, summary?, error?}.

USER INPUTS: the only input is RunRequest {message (max 200000 chars), run_id optional, mode:'standard'|'embedded'}. The user does NOT supply the parent BC name/URI directly in the API contract; the LLM infers parent_entity_key from the message against the registry menu. GET /api/entities serves the registered parent list (durable store first, in-memory fallback) so the frontend can show choices.

The frontend presumably lets the user reference a parent by name inside the free-text prompt (registry descriptions exist 'shown to the LLM for matching'); no separate parent-selection request field exists on the wire.

DIVERGENCES from standalone (14 steps): embedded (7-8 steps) drops form planning/building/saving (standalone 5-7, viewMetadataV2), event handler plan/write/compile/register (standalone 8-11, eventhandler endpoint, TS/JS), lookup detection (Phase 11), and duplicate-name fast-fail; it adds the BERelation step and the child-PK-trio field discipline; view registration becomes opt-in instead of always; deploy is split into two user-visible steps (warnings check + deploy) instead of one step with sub-steps 4a/4b; deploy datastore URI differs (embedded passes dataStoreURI 'urn:datastore:com.extensions.extension' in stepB).

ERROR HANDLING pattern: every step wraps its work in try/except; any exception or is_qad_success failure yields an SSE 'error' event and returns (terminating the generator); the only retry anywhere is the single VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR-driven re-POST of step 3; step 6's QAD response is the only unchecked write.

VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR (shared with standalone) claims it can fix: duplicate BC name (rename), field code conflicts, bc_pascal >32 chars, reserved-word field names, missing maxLength, dataType mismatch; cannot fix auth/timeout/permission errors; output either {status:'fixed', fix_summary, spec} or {status:'failed', reason}.

Untracked script probe_parent_eh.py probes updating an EXISTING parent view event handler: GET eventhandler?appURI=urn:app:com.extensions.customapp&viewURI=urn:view:viewmeta:com.qad.erp.sales.SalesOrders&eventHandlerType=BEFORE&appliesTo=WEB, then POST eventhandler back with {supplementaryMessages:[], eventHandlerV2s:[{uri, appURI, viewURI, eventHandlerType, appliesTo, isActive, concurrencyHash (from GET), typeScriptCode, javaScriptCode, mappingCode, disallowedActions}]}, with a fallback shape omitting uri; it verifies concurrencyHash changes after update. Not wired into any pipeline.

Child PK fallback insert position (index 2) silently assumes the LLM put domaincodeEx and the FK at indices 0-1; if it did not, the injected PK lands mid-list (ordering only affects primaryKey ordinals and column order, not correctness of the FK-vs-PK constraint).

pipeline_embedded_2_2_2_2_2.summary: AUX's embedded (client-extension / parent-BC) flow lives entirely inside the Client Extensions feature pane (D:/WEB_AUX/aux_web_version/frontend/src/features/client_ext/). There is no separate route or screen for embedded mode: the same ClientExtPanel chat-style UI serves both cases, and the ONLY embedded-specific user input is a two-option SegmentedToggle ("Standard BC" / "Embedded BC") shown on the empty state, plus the free-text prompt. Submitting fires a single POST /api/run {message, mode} SSE stream that runs the entire embedded pipeline (requirements LLM -> field LLM -> metadata POST -> auto-fix -> BERelation -> warnings check -> deploy -> optional standalone view) in one shot with ZERO human gates: the user never approves fields, never picks the parent BC (an LLM chooses it from the server-side entity registry), never sees a dry-run, and only learns of a wrong parent choice via a terminal SSE error. Progress is a read-only 7-row step rail (ProgressPanel) whose labels are hardcoded client-side and have drifted from the backend's labels; the backend's optional step 8 (standalone view registration) and its 'warning' SSE events are silently invisible in the UI. On success a SummaryCard shows BC name/description/module/PKs/fields but omits the parent entity even though the embedded summary payload carries parent_entity, and it displays the stale hardcoded module com.extensions.customapp. A read-only "Registered BCs" page (GET /api/entities) lists builtin QAD parents and custom parents auto-registered as a side effect of standard-mode runs; there is no UI to add/edit parents or to select one for a run. Supporting surfaces are run history (list/detail/delete), a status-only Settings page, health chip, and JWT login. UX strengths worth keeping: mounted-pane state survival across feature switches, abort-on-new-run, guarded view updates so mid-run navigation isn't yanked back, and a triple-fallback summary recovery (state, ref, history refetch). UX weaknesses vs Adaptive's 7-stage gated rail: no gating/approval at all, no dry-run vs live labeling, LLM-chosen parent, invisible warnings/step 8, drifted duplicate step labels, no HTTP error handling on the SSE fetch (a 429/500 ends the run silently), and an attach button still offered in embedded mode although the backend ignores attachments there.

docs.summary: The three guides define QAD's official vocabulary and procedure for the embedded/extension case. Per Class 3, an "Extension" is not a special object type: it is a normal Business Component created with the "Embedded" checkbox checked, plus a "Relationship" record of Relationship Type "Child" whose Source is the child/extension BC and whose Related BC is the parent, with a Field Mapping that maps the child's copy of the parent key fields to the parent's keys. Cardinality is auto-identified by the platform: Many-to-One (child has extra primary keys beyond the parent's) renders on the parent form as an embedded grid; One-to-One (identical key sets, mapping auto-filled) renders as a panel of fields; both also appear as tabs in the parent's top navigation. For an Embedded BC you deliberately skip Form, Browse, and View creation - the platform builds the grid/panel automatically and embedded BCs never appear on the menu - so the Case 2 pipeline is BC(embedded) + fields + relationship/field-mapping + deploy, dropping Case 1's form/view/browse/menu stages. A third variant, the "Non-Embedded Grid," is a full standalone BC (own Form/Browse/View) additionally attached to a parent via a Child relationship with "Include Grid on Parent Form" checked, which unlocks an "Edit Grid" button on the child BC's Form panel. Class 3 also covers the two other relationship-family features: Lookup Relations (per-field "Lookup" checkbox pointing at a related BC + browse, auto-populating related display fields) and Formula Fields (Formula checkbox + expression editor; cross-relationship field references use the pattern _com_extensions_training_Students.score, and calculation depends on the Activity Feeds OS script). Class 6 covers server-side "Java Extensions" (JEF): a Maven/Java-17 project managed by the qad-java-sse VS Code plugin (Init app / Update app dependency / Build and Deploy / Undeploy) whose @Extension class extends the generated <BC>BaseService and overrides initialize/create/update, connecting to the environment at https://<host>/clouderp with a Client ID plus Developer-role user credentials. Class 7 covers client-side "Event Handlers": TypeScript compiled to JavaScript and stored in the database, attached in the BC's Form panel Event Handlers grid with Timing Primary/Pre/Post, base classes QraViewTSHandlerWithViewFormTSHandler / QraViewFormTSHandlerV2 / ViewGridTSHandlerV2 / QraBrowseTSHandlerV2, and runtime data access via this.NgData where extension data is reached as this.NgData._com_extensions_training_CountryExtension[0].knownFor (module URI with underscores + BC name, camelCase field names - matching the known camelCase-wire/PascalCase-field-code split). The guides show UI screens only; no REST wire captures for creating relationships exist in them, so wire payload shapes for Case 2 must come from AUX code or live network capture. All com.extensions.training / com.extensions.extension identifiers in the guides are training-environment values that map to com.yash.digwish / urn:datastore:com.yash.extension in the new environment.

facts.fact: Extensions are the way to add additional information into an existing business component; the platform supports different extension types for different scenarios.
A Many-to-One extension is represented on the parent screen as an embedded grid; a One-to-One extension is represented as a panel of fields.
Official step 1 for an extension: create a New Business Component and check the 'Embedded' checkbox, which means the extension will not appear on the menu and is accessible only from the parent BC.
The extension BC's Main screen is the standard BC screen (Business Component, Type: Standard, Label, Physical Table, Description, Scope, URIs); the guide sets Scope to System.
BC Options checkboxes are: Embedded, Approvals, Business Document, Not Extensible.
Extension field definitions are created with the Fields panel's Import function from an Excel spreadsheet (Data Source Type: File), same as a standalone BC.

A Many-to-One child extension's primary key must include the parent's key fields plus its own distinguishing keys (Students PK: 1 ClassName, 2 Location, 3 LastName, 4 FirstName over parent Training's ClassName+Location).
If the parent BC has a key field that could be empty, the corresponding key field in the extension must have its Required checkbox unchecked.

Step 2: on the child BC's screen scroll to the Relationships panel and click New; the Relationships grid columns are Relationship, Relationship Label, Source Business Component, Related Business Component.

Relationship Main screen field names: Source Business Component, Source App (shows urn:app:...), Related Business Component, Related App, Relationship, Relationship Label, Relationship Type (value 'Child'), Cardinality; plus section 'Composition Relation' (checkboxes Composition Relation, Cascade Delete) and section 'Include Grid on Parent Form' (checkboxes Include Grid on Parent Form, Cascade Delete).
The relationship is authored FROM the child extension (Source = extension BC) pointing AT the parent (Related = parent BC), with Relationship Type = Child; the Related BC is chosen via a search icon.
The Related Business Component search dialog defaults to filter 'Embedded equals No' because Embedded Business Components cannot themselves be extended.
The system auto-identifies the Cardinality (e.g. 'Many to one'); as a result the extension is included into the parent's form as an embedded grid.

Field Mapping links child records to their parent: for each source (child) field a search icon opens the child's key-field list, and you map child key -> parent key (e.g. ClassName->ClassName, Location->Location); the grid columns are Source, Field/Literal, Related.
Field Mapping supports a Field/Literal column, i.e. a mapping row can be a literal value rather than a field.

For an Embedded (Many-to-One) extension you do NOT build a Form (the system builds the grid automatically) and do NOT create a View (extensions are not menu-accessible, they are 'Embedded' in the parent BC); no Browse is created either.

Step 3: deploy the extension BC itself: Deployment panel, Data Store URI selected via search icon (training value urn:datastore:com.extensions.extension), datastore must be in Development mode, click Deploy. The parent BC is not redeployed.
After deploy, opening the parent from the menu shows the extension; a page refresh may be needed before the extension grid/panel appears.
After deployment, the extension appears both as a grid at the bottom of the parent page and as a tab in the parent's Top Navigation (e.g. Main | Country Industries | Country Extension).

One-to-One extension: created identically (new BC + Embedded checked) but its primary key is exactly the parent's key (CountryCode only); the platform then auto-identifies the relation as Child with One-to-One cardinality and auto-fills the Field Mapping because child and parent key fields are identical.

Non-Embedded Grid variant: a BC created WITHOUT the Embedded checkbox must have Form, Browse and View built before deployment; it is then attached to a parent via a Child relationship with 'Include Grid on Parent Form' checked.

Once a relationship with 'Include Grid on Parent Form' exists, the child BC's Form panel gains an 'Edit Grid' button to configure the grid representation (column order, hiding columns via 'Change Grid Definition').

Non-Embedded Grid capabilities: accessible from the main menu through its own View/Form as well as through grids on parent BCs; can have more than one parent BC; can hold records unrelated to any parent.
QAD names exactly two relationship types: Child Relationships and Lookup Relationships; the Child relation covers non-embedded grids, embedded-grid extensions, and one-to-one extensions.
Browse URI pattern: urn:browse:bebrowse:<module>.<name> (e.g. urn:browse:bebrowse:com.extensions.training.trainingRo..., urn:browse:bebrowse:com.extensions.training.countries).
Standard-BC URI patterns: urn:be:<package>.I<Entity> for Standard BCs (e.g. urn:be:com.qad.base.address.ICountry) and urn:service:<package>.I<Service>-<Name> for Action BCs.

A parent browse can include fields from a one-to-one extension: in browse Fields click Select, the 'Select Relationship' dialog shows the relationship hierarchy; expand the parent BC line, select the extension relationship, Continue, then pick extension fields.

Lookup Relation procedure: add a field to the BC, open its Details, check the Lookup checkbox, search/select the Related Business Component, the platform auto-identifies the field mapping, then choose the Browse used by the lookup, click OK/Close/Save, and REDEPLOY the BC for the new field to apply.
The Lookup config panel contains: Related Business Component, Browse, Relationship, Relationship Label, and a 'Visualize as Drop-Down List' checkbox.

A field with a Lookup relation automatically gets Lookup and Drill-down icons on the form, and related display fields (e.g. CountryDescription) can be placed on the form read-only and auto-populate without coding.

If a BC character field's physical name matches a Generalized Codes field name, the platform automatically converts it to a drop-down; after adding Generalized Codes values the cache must be cleared via browser console $.post("api/webshell/clearAllCaches").

Formula Fields: check the Formula checkbox on the field, then in field Details use the Formula editor with 'Include Operator' (e.g. AVERAGE, COUNT) and 'Include Field', which opens the same Select Relationship hierarchy to pick a child-BC field.

Formula expressions reference fields across a relationship with the pattern AVERAGE([_com_extensions_training_Students.score]) - underscore-prefixed module URI with dots replaced by underscores, then BC name, then camelCase field name (field CODE is 'Score', reference is 'score').

Formula Fields are computed via the Activity Feeds mechanism; if inactive, run OS Script 'activity_feed_update' from the OS Scripts screen (Actions > Execute Script), which sends an inbox notification when done.

Embedded-grid extension data is included in parent Export/Import by default; a non-embedded grid has its own CRUD and is NOT included until the parent BC's 'Business Document' checkbox is enabled, after which a Business Document panel appears and the non-embedded grid becomes exportable.

Business Document URI pattern is urn:bd:<module>.<BC>.<BC> (urn:bd:com.extensions.training.Training.Training); the Business Document panel's Drill-Down Links > 'Business Document API Documentation' > Open > 'Open API Documentation' shows REST API definitions with GET, POST, DELETE, HEAD, PATCH and Query endpoints per CRUD action.

The Java Extension Framework (JEF) is the server-side mechanism to inject custom logic into the BC lifecycle; extensions can modify or completely override default BC behavior, work for both platform and coded BCs, and are upgrade-safe because they are separate from core QAD.

JEF runtime flow: Web UI save -> Progress BL -> if a Java Extension exists for the BC, BL triggers the overridden method (e.g. create) in the JEF; extension code calls back via super.create() to complete the standard flow.

Java Extensions are Maven-based Java projects developed in VS Code with the 'qad-java-sse-vscode-x.x.x.vsix' plugin ('sse' = server-side extension; project artifact named training-server-side-extension); plugin commands are 'QAD Extension: Init app', 'Update app dependency', 'Build and Deploy', 'Undeploy'.

JEF Init app flow prompts, in order: environment URL (format https://<host>/clouderp, obtained from My Developer Settings 'VS Code Plugin Connection URL'), Client ID (from the Client IDs management page or the environment Administrator), then webui username and password - the user must have the Developer role - then a picker listing apps into which the extension may be added.

The generated JEF project folder is named after the app URI with underscores (urn_app_com.extensions.training) and contains config, data, lib, src, target, .gitignore, pom.xml; 'Update app dependency' pulls in generated service classes for every BC in the app.

A JEF extension class is annotated @Extension and extends the generated <BC>BaseService (e.g. TrainingBaseService); it overrides initialize(Output<TrainingDataSet>), create(InputOutput<TrainingDataSet>), update(InputOutput<TrainingDataSet>), all throwing BCExecutionError; imports come from <module>.<bc lowercase>.<BC>DataSet/<BC>Record and com.qad.ipc.dto.{BCExecutionError,InputOutput}; validation uses this.addValidationError(msg) + throwAddedValidationErrors(); record access via dsTraining.getValue().getTtTraining()[0].

Build produces <module>-ext-cust.jar (com.extensions.training-ext-cust.jar) via mvn clean package, deployed by the plugin; JEF validation errors surface in the UI Errors grid with an Error ID prefixed 'JEF'.

JEF helper APIs allow: executing SQL queries, reading session context (current user ID, role, domain), fetching translations, logging to the extension log file, and making HTTP calls to external services; JEF requires Java 17 and Maven.
An Event Handler is TypeScript compiled into JavaScript and saved to the database, assigned to a business component and executed on the front-end for the corresponding UI.

Event handler Timing/run order values: Primary (default for TS handlers in coded BCs), Pre (runs before Primary or coded handler), Post (runs after); the Timing dropdown becomes selectable when adding a handler to a standard QAD BC, where the guide selects Post.

Event handler types: View TS handler (page lifecycle, main handler and starting point for the others), ViewForm handler (form element UI events), ViewGrid handler (grid lifecycle and control events), Browse handler (browse record selection and toolbar/Actions clicks).

Event handler base classes: QraViewTSHandlerWithViewFormTSHandler (View TS), QraViewFormTSHandlerV2 (ViewForm), ViewGridTSHandlerV2 (ViewGrid), QraBrowseTSHandlerV2 (Browse), imported from the Qad.QraView.TSHandler namespace.

Event handlers are managed on the BC screen's Form panel in an 'Event Handlers' grid with columns Timing, Active, Applies To, App, App URI (Applies To value 'Web'); create with New, edit with Details; the editor has Compile, Save, Close buttons; the Active checkbox must be checked, and after saving the handler the Business Component itself must be saved.

Handler module naming encodes owner-app and timing: on a standard QAD BC extended by app training, module com.qad.erp.base.EventHandler.Country.ComExtensionsTraining.Maint_BEFORE (Pre) / Maint_AFTER (Post); on the app's own BC, module com.extensions.training.EventHandler.Training.ComExtensionsTraining.Maint_PRIMARY; the generated Maint handler class name must not be changed or the handler stops running.

In a handler, this.NgData holds the selected record's data; the parent record is always element 0 (this.NgData.trainings[0]) and wire field names are camelCase (studentCount, capacity, knownFor, industry).

A parent BC's event handler reaches embedded-extension data via this.NgData._com_extensions_training_CountryExtension[0].knownFor and this.NgData._com_extensions_training_CountryIndustries (array) - the same underscore-module prefix pattern used by formula fields.

pipeline_embedded_2_2_2_2_2_2.summary: PHASE0_AUDIT.md (4879 lines, dated 2026-08-06) already contains a full, mostly-verified inventory of AUX's embedded (Case 2) flow. Section A2 (verified, verdict minor-issues) documents the entire embedded pipeline: same POST /api/run entry with mode=="embedded" dispatch, 7 steps (8 with wants_separate_view), 2-3 LLM calls, and exactly six QAD-mutating call shapes; it establishes that embedded creates a data-extension BC + one MANYTOONE BERelation + deploy, and creates NO form, NO event handler, NO TypeScript, NO lookups, and never registers the child as a future parent. Parent identity comes from a hardcoded 5-entry local registry chosen by the LLM, never validated against live QAD. The audit's verification appendix (Part V) corrected the read-back story: backend/probe_parent_eh.py (untracked) already GETs an existing parent-view event handler (SalesOrders) and POSTs it back as an update using concurrencyHash optimistic locking, which retired the "recover urn:be: by network capture" deferral and left one open item, Q-L: whether that probe was ever actually run (QUESTIONS.md:284). A11 (NOT verified) covers the uncommitted lookup_detector/lookup_generator/progress_parser work: all three are load-bearing untracked files, the lookups POST is permanently dry-run gated, and none of it touches the embedded pipeline (the router skips the parser for embedded mode). Sections A8, A9, A10, A11, B1, B2, B3, B4 never received the citation-verification pass and the completeness critic never ran, so line numbers in those sections should be re-opened before Phase-code depends on them. Endpoint provenance for Case 2 is fully recorded in A4 (verified): rows 4/5/6 (entitymetadatas create/GET/patch), 10 (berelation, embedded-only), 11/12 (deployCheckForWarnings/deployBusinessEntity), 9 (viewResourceMetadatas, optional), all on the {BASE}/qad-central/api/qracore/ prefix that is stale for the new environment, plus the probe's row-16 GET eventhandler shape. Every identity literal (com.extensions.customapp, urn:datastore:com.extensions.extension, /qad-central/) is enumerated in the A4.3 work-list and is stale by definition for the com.yash.digwish target.

facts.fact: Embedded (Case 2) is a mode dispatch inside the same POST /api/run route: run_embedded_pipeline(req.message) is selected when req.mode == 'embedded'; only req.message is passed (no parsed_requirements, no lookup_candidates).
Embedded mode explicitly bypasses the Progress (.p/.cls) parser: `if req.mode != "embedded":` at client_extensions.py:129, with recorded reason 'it picks a parent entity from a fixed registry'.
Embedded step count is dynamic: BASE_TOTAL_STEPS = 7 (pipeline_embedded.py:30), raised to 8 when wants_separate_view is true (:104-105).

Embedded ordered step inventory: 1 requirements (LLM+registry), 2 field design (LLM+PK guard), 3 entitymetadatas POST, 4 conditional auto-fix retry, 3.5 dropdown wiring (re-emits step id 3), 5 berelation POST, 6 deployCheckForWarnings, 7 deployBusinessEntity, 8 optional viewResourceMetadatas.
An embedded run makes 2 LLM calls (EMBEDDED_REQUIREMENTS_GATHERING, EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR), or 3 if step-4 VALIDATOR_AND_CORRECTOR triggers; the rate-limit comment claiming '8 LLM calls' is stale.

Parent-BC identity is chosen by the LLM from an {ENTITY_MENU} injected into the prompt, then resolved via get_entity() against the in-process QAD_STANDARD_ENTITIES cache seeded from 5 hardcoded built-ins (SalesOrderHeaders, PurchaseOrderHeaders, ItemMaster, InventoryMaster, WorkOrderMaster) and overlaid at startup from the DB parent_entities table via hydrate().

Parent info is used for exactly five things: fk_field/fk_type into step-2 input, fk_codes exclusion set for the child-PK guard, relation payload args, parent domain-field guess inside the builder, and user-facing messages/summary. It is never validated against live QAD and never used to select a handler target, form, or view.

Embedded creates NO form/panel layout (build_form_payload never imported; viewMetadataV2 absent), NO event handler, NO TypeScript, NO lookups, and NO registry self-registration (register_and_persist_custom_bc absent) - an embedded child never becomes selectable as a parent.

Grid-only: BERelation is written with cardinality MANYTOONE, isEmbedded False, isIncludeOnParent False, isUseInBusinessDocument True; a dated in-code finding (2026-07-15) records that live tests proved the Composition-Relation/Include-Grid flags cannot make it render as a panel; a panel requires a ONETOONE redesign (child PK = domaincodeEx + parent FK only).

That the deployed artifact renders as a grid on the parent form is QAD runtime behaviour relied on from the authors' recorded live test (PROGRESS.md:186-189, PanelTest/PanelTestPavan), not verifiable from source.
Mandated PK ordering in EMBEDDED_FIELD_CREATOR: 1 domaincodeEx, 2 <fk_field>, 3 <child_pk.code>; a deterministic guard inserts a fallback child PK at index 2 if the LLM omitted one.

BERelation payload has exactly two BERelationFields mappings (domaincodeEx -> parent domain field, fk_field -> fk_field); the parent's domain field name is guessed from the local registry pk_fields (first entry containing 'domain', default 'DomainCode'), not read from QAD.
relationID is partially hardcoded: '8c9676c6-0c12-13a3-f114-' + 12 hex chars of a fresh uuid4 (embedded_builder.py:278).
